problems.title: Teacher-forced PCR does not establish small distributional changes
problems.source_location: PDF pp.2–3 Eq 1–2; Appendix C.1 p.26
claim: The preliminary PCR study motivates the hypothesis that RL changes probabilities mainly at a small set of reasoning-related tokens.
analysis: Take a vocabulary of \(100\) tokens. Let two next-token laws be \[p=(0.02,0.98/99,\ldots,0.98/99)\] and \[q=(0.99,0.01/99,\ldots,0.01/99)\]. Both have the same unique argmax, but \(\|p-q\|_{\rm TV}=0.97\). Repeating this construction on every teacher-forced prefix gives perfect argmax preservation while distributional change remains large. Teacher-forced prefixes also differ from prefixes generated by a model's own earlier tokens.
result: Identical teacher-forced argmax decisions do not establish small probability changes or free-running path agreement. The paper presents a motivating hypothesis, not a formal total-variation or knowledge-preservation theorem; the counterexample limits that interpretation without refuting measured reasoning gains.
assumptions: Only the author-released source version and stated claim are assessed.
repair: Describe conditional top \(1\) agreement; measure distributions/likelihood and perform controlled token-position interventions.
problems.impact_rationale: PCR is an empirical argmax diagnostic used to motivate a hypothesis. The counterexample shows it is insufficient evidence for a stronger distributional interpretation, not that a claimed formal guarantee or the core measured transfer result is false.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: Raw logit-difference cosine is not invariant to probability-preserving shifts
claim: Raw logit-difference cosine identifies probability-distribution alignment.
analysis: Let centered logit differences be \(a=(1,-1,0)\) and \(b=(1,0,-1)\), with cosine \(1/2\). Adding a common scalar to all logits preserves each softmax law, yet large same-sign or opposite-sign constant shifts make the raw difference cosine approach \(1\) or \(-1\). Thus this cosine is not determined by the probability laws.
result: This is a scope/provenance gap, not proof that the stronger empirical conclusion is false.
assumptions: Only the author-released source version and stated claim are assessed.
repair: Center logit differences or use explicit probability/log-ratio metrics; align semantic vocabulary and report model/trajectory uncertainty.
problems.impact_rationale: The available evidence does not settle this concern, so it does not contribute to the paper's impact label.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: Cosine analysis cumulatively duplicates answer prefixes
claim: The cosine-analysis loop advances prefixes one token at a time.
analysis: The author similarity loop appends the accumulating answer prefix repeatedly. For an initial context of length \(2\), it produces prefix lengths \(2,3,5,8\), rather than \(2,3,4,5\). The evaluated sequences therefore repeat earlier answer tokens; this is a local analysis-script defect, not an estimate of corrected paper conclusions.
result: The bounded local discrepancy or counterexample is supported; no change in published benchmark scores is quantified.
assumptions: Only the author-released source version and stated claim are assessed.
repair: Keep prompt_ids immutable and append answer[: i] to it, or increment cached prefix by one token.
problems.impact_rationale: This establishes the stated local correction or limitation. A consequential failure of the paper's central result has not been demonstrated.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: PCR coefficient shadowing, denominator mismatch and one-run averaging
claim: PCR uses the supplied coefficient and correct position/run denominators.
analysis: The coefficient argument named i is overwritten by a loop index of the same name. In addition, a sequence with \(99\) perfectly preserved checked predictions is divided by \(100\), and the averaging branch runs only range(\(1\)), yielding a single value with zero reported spread. These contracts do not implement the intended coefficient, denominator and repeated-run summary.
result: The bounded local discrepancy or counterexample is supported; no change in published benchmark scores is quantified.
assumptions: Only the author-released source version and stated claim are assessed.
repair: Separate lambda and token index, normalize valid positions, explicitly load \(32\) unique aligned run files and publish exact producing scripts.

problems.title: Decoding and prompt controls confound recovery interpretation
problems.source_location: PDF p.5 Table 1 caption/footnote; p.25 Table 5/Appendix A.2; vllm/tests/RAST_decode/run.py:54–60
claim: The decoding/prompt controls isolate the claimed recovery effect.
analysis: Table 1 and Appendix A disclose greedy base decoding versus temperature-\(1\), top-\(p=0.95\) RAST/RL sampling. Thus the recovery ratio compares complete systems and does not isolate the logit adjustment under a common decoding policy. Figure 6 gives approximately \(70.5\) on MATH500 at \(\lambda=0\) with sampling, versus the table’s greedy base \(68.6\); this is illustrative, not an exact decomposition of every gain. The dagger note and Appendix A.2 give differing descriptions of the small-model prompt, while the current run.py fixes use_chat to false. The producing run configuration is required to settle prompt attribution.
result: This is a scope/provenance gap, not proof that the stronger empirical conclusion is false.
assumptions: Only the author-released source version and stated claim are assessed.
repair: Report all-greedy and matched-sampling panels; publish exact input strings and decoding configs per model.
problems.impact_rationale: The available evidence does not settle this concern, so it does not contribute to the paper's impact label.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: GRPO resource model includes critic and inconsistent CPU arithmetic
problems.source_location: PDF p.29 AppendixD; p.8 Table 4; original DeepSeekMath §4.1.1
claim: The resource model correctly accounts for GRPO components and optimizer memory.
analysis: GRPO does not require a learned critic. The stated CPU-memory arithmetic for two FP32 Adam state arrays, \(14\times10^9\) parameters and three models is \(2\cdot14\times10^9\cdot4\cdot3=336\times10^9\) bytes, not \(156\) GB. Counting optimizer states for frozen models also needs justification. This corrects the resource model rather than measuring the actual runtime/memory of any run.
result: The bounded local discrepancy or counterexample is supported; no change in published benchmark scores is quantified.
assumptions: Only the author-released source version and stated claim are assessed.
repair: Profile actual active copies/trainable states by phase, separate CPU/GPU, rollout/reference/old-policy and activations, and recompute savings.

problems.title: Throughput reduction confused with latency increase
problems.source_location: PDF p.8 Table 4 and inference-speed paragraph
claim: A throughput reduction equals the stated latency increase.
analysis: For equal generated-token counts and comparable hardware/batching, generation time is inversely proportional to throughput. The current Table 4 rates give RAST time increases \(243.1/200.3-1\approx21.37\%\), \(243.1/202.7-1\approx19.93\%\), and \(249.5/216.1-1\approx15.46\%\). The corresponding throughput reductions are \(17.61\%\), \(16.62\%\), and \(13.39\%\). These do not yield the stated \(13\)–\(16\%\) latency range. This is an equal-work arithmetic correction, not an independent measurement of request latency; actual output lengths, queueing and prompt processing also matter.
result: The bounded local discrepancy or counterexample is supported; no change in published benchmark scores is quantified.
assumptions: Only the author-released source version and stated claim are assessed.
repair: Report throughput as throughput or use inverse-rate conversion for equal workload; measure end-to-end latency on matched requests.
problems.impact_rationale: This establishes the stated local correction or limitation. A consequential failure of the paper's central result has not been demonstrated.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: Uncertainty, lexical proxy, transfer scope and benchmark versions need stronger specification
claim: The reported uncertainty and proxies establish the claimed general transfer.
analysis: The repeated generations share benchmark questions, so \(32\) runs are not \(32\) independent benchmark samples. The paper does show standard-deviation information in Figure 6; a claim of no uncertainty reporting anywhere would be false. The author reasoning_tokens.py averages keyword occurrences per response, rather than per output token. Different response lengths can therefore contribute to the reported lexical differences, and broad words such as “but” are imperfect behavioral proxies. The experiments transfer across scales within Qwen and within Llama; they do not establish arbitrary transfer between incompatible tokenizers. LiveCodeBench is described by a count of \(880\) questions without a fully frozen release/window. These are limits on statistical, mechanism and version attribution, not demonstrated data contamination.
result: This is a scope/provenance gap, not proof that the stronger empirical conclusion is false.
assumptions: Only the author-released source version and stated claim are assessed.
repair: Publish paired prompt-level uncertainty, length-adjusted/semantic behavior measures, versioned benchmark IDs and explicit tokenizer assumptions.
problems.impact_rationale: The available evidence does not settle this concern, so it does not contribute to the paper's impact label.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.
